items.title: Gravity and quantum information linked through a derivation of Einstein's equations
items.abstract: Recent research shows that gravity and quantum information are deeply connected and that the shape of spacetime can be traced back to the way information is stored in quantum fields.

items.title: One step closer to quantum computers that can correct their own mistakes
items.abstract: Researchers from Rutgers, IBM and collaborating institutions have shown that a quantum computer can check what is happening inside it and respond while it is running, repeatedly resetting parts of the system to bring chaotic behavior under control.

items.title: Hybrid quantum computers could finally get to grips with light and matter
items.abstract: Many of nature's most important processes depend on how particles of matter interact with light and other force-carrying particles. So far, however, it has proven difficult for conventional computers to determine how individual particles behave in these interactions.

items.title: Award-winning microscopy image disqualified over AI use
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03240-7 The incident has prompted discussions about the use of artificial intelligence in scientific imagery.

items.title: Author Correction: Timing and trajectory of BCR::ABL1 -driven chronic myeloid leukaemia
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11253-5 Author Correction: Timing and trajectory of BCR::ABL1 -driven chronic myeloid leukaemia

items.title: Keep medical doctors in academia — without them, health-care research will suffer
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03225-6 Better career support and more funding stability is needed to retain this invaluable group of scientists.

items.title: Economics Nobel awarded for work on stabilizing economies in crisis
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03251-4 Laureates share award that builds on the theories that contributed to governments intervening during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Beyond the solvent fog: watching molecules dance in the crowd
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02970-y A technique called time-resolved X-ray liquidography has been used to shed precision light on the steps involved in a classic chemical reaction.

items.title: What does a PhD pay? Data reveal huge gaps across Europe
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03181-1 Earnings come in a combination of scholarships and salaries and vary widely between countries, an analysis by international federation Eurodoc reveals.

items.title: Hidden signals in sleep can predict future health
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03207-8 From a single night of sleep, AI tools can uncover physiological patterns linked to disease and mortality that are missed by conventional sleep measures.

items.title: I told ChatGPT to ‘continue’ — it went too far
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02714-y An ambiguous instruction caused the chatbot to send three e-mails from Ying Zhao’s connected account. The incident advanced Zhao’s project, but showed that chatbots need limits.

items.title: Does the decline of book reading mark the end of rational thinking?
items.abstract: Nature, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03224-7 Smartphones and artificial intelligence are undermining our ability to follow a complex argument, with grave consequences.
